question.prompt: The smallest product one could obtain by multiplying two numbers in the set \(\{ -7, -5, -1, 1, 3 \}\) is

solutions.explanation:
Multiplying two numbers with the same sign gives a positive product, while opposite signs give a negative product. Since negative products are possible, the smallest product must use one negative number and one positive number.

Among negative numbers, the one with the greatest absolute value is smallest. The available negative factors have absolute values at most \(7\), and the positive factors are at most \(3\). Thus a negative product has absolute value at most \(7\cdot3=21\). This is attained by
\[(-7)(3)=-21.\]
Therefore the smallest product is \(-21\), choice B.
solutions.title: Choose the most negative product
